sub: In 1471, Đại Việt took Vijaya, the Cham capital. But that was not the end of Champa.
say: In fourteen seventy-one, Dye Vee-et took Vee-jaya, the Chahm capital. But that was not the end of Chahm-pah.

title: THE SOUTH
sub: Further south, smaller Cham kingdoms survived.
say: Further south, smaller Chahm kingdoms survived.

title: STEP BY STEP
sub: The Nguyễn lords moved their frontier step by step: Phú Yên around 1611, Kauthara in 1653.
say: The Nwin lords moved their frontier step by step: Foo Yen around sixteen eleven, Kow-tah-rah in sixteen fifty-three.

title: PANDURANGA
sub: In the 1690s they took Panduranga, the last Cham principality. After resistance, they let a Cham ruler govern it again, under Nguyễn authority.
say: In the sixteen-nineties they took Pahn-doo-rahng-gah, the last Chahm principality. After resistance, they let a Chahm ruler govern it again, under Nwin authority.

sub: In 1832, Emperor Minh Mạng brought Panduranga under direct rule, as a province of Vietnam.
say: In eighteen thirty-two, Emperor Min Mahng brought Pahn-doo-rahng-gah under direct rule, as a province of Vietnam.

sub: Revolts followed, and were put down by 1835.
say: Revolts followed, and were put down by eighteen thirty-five.

title: WHAT REMAINS?
sub: The state was gone. So what is left of Champa today?
say: The state was gone. So what is left of Chahm-pah today?
